events.title: Rise of Kingdom of Sheba
events.description: Ancient Yemen saw the Kingdom of Sheba, enriched by spice trade. Sheba was the starting point of the 'Incense Road,' transporting frankincense and myrrh from South Arabia to the Mediterranean. The biblical story of the Queen of Sheba visiting King Solomon reflects Sheba's wealth and prestige. The Marib Dam was an ancient engineering marvel.

events.title: Sheba Kingdom Golden Age
events.description: Kingdom of Sheba reached zenith, controlling spice trade. Capital Marib prospered, building massive dam irrigating farmland. Sabaean civilization developed advanced architecture, irrigation and writing systems.

events.title: Himyarite Kingdom
events.description: Himyarite Kingdom replaced Sheba, unifying South Arabia. Kingdom continued prospering from trade, capital Zafar became cultural center. Himyarite kings later converted to Judaism, unique in Arab world.

events.title: Ethiopian-Persian Conquest
events.description: Christian Ethiopia invaded Yemen, overthrowing Himyarite Kingdom. Subsequently Persian Sassanid dynasty conquered Yemen, ruling until Islamic conquest. Legend says Prophet Muhammad was born in 'Year of Elephant' (Ethiopian failed attack on Mecca).

events.title: Yemen Converts to Islam
events.description: Persian governor and Yemeni tribes accepted Islam, peacefully submitting to Prophet Muhammad. Yemen became part of Islamic Caliphate. Many Yemenis participated in Islamic conquests, settling in Egypt and North Africa.

events.title: Zaydi Imamate Established
events.description: Zaydi Shia Muslims established Imamate in northern Yemen, ruling over a thousand years (until 1962). Zaydism is moderate Shia, close to Sunni. Imam rule shaped northern Yemen's political and religious character.

events.title: Sulayhid Dynasty
events.description: Fatimid Caliphate supported Sulayhid dynasty ruling Yemen, spreading Ismaili Islam. Dynasty promoted trade and culture, Aden became Indian Ocean trade hub. Famous Queen Arwa ruled about 40 years.

events.title: Rasulid Dynasty
events.description: Rasulid Sultanate ruled southern and western Yemen for over 200 years, this was prosperous period in Yemen's history. Dynasty promoted agriculture, architecture and scholarship, Zabid became Islamic learning center.

events.title: First Ottoman Occupation
events.description: Ottoman Empire conquered Yemen's coastal regions, contesting control with Zaydi Imams. Ottomans controlled major ports like Aden and Hodeidah, but highlands remained under Imam rule. Ottoman-Zaydi conflict continued intermittently.

events.title: Expulsion of Ottomans
events.description: Zaydi Imam Qasim the Great expelled Ottomans, unifying Yemen. This was strong unified period in Yemen's history. Imamate expanded to include Hadramaut, Yemen experienced relative peace and prosperity.

events.title: British Occupation of Aden
events.description: Britain occupied Aden port citing protection of route to India. Aden became British colony, developing as important coaling station and commercial center. Britain established Aden Protectorate, signing treaties with interior tribes but not directly ruling.

events.title: Yemen Civil War and Division
events.description: Zaydi Imamate internal factional fighting and civil war led to national division and weakening. Tribal autonomy increased, central authority weakened.

events.title: Ottoman Re-occupation
events.description: Ottoman Empire second conquest of northern Yemen, establishing Yemen Province. Ottomans controlled lowlands and cities, but highland tribes and Zaydi Imams continued resistance.

events.title: Yahya Uprising
events.description: Zaydi Imam Yahya launched prolonged uprising against Ottoman rule. After years of guerrilla warfare, Yahya forced Ottomans to recognize his autonomy over highlands.

events.title: Mutawakkilite Kingdom of Yemen Independence
events.description: After WWI Ottoman Empire collapsed, Imam Yahya declared Mutawakkilite Kingdom of Yemen independent. Yahya ruled northern Yemen, adopting isolationist policy, resisting modernization, maintaining traditional Zaydi rule.

events.title: Yemen-Saudi War
events.description: Yemen and Saudi Arabia fought border war, Yemen defeated. Treaty of Taif ceded Yemen's northern territories to Saudi, establishing modern borders. This strengthened Saudi influence over Yemeni affairs.

events.title: Joined Arab Federation
events.description: Imam Ahmad brought North Yemen into Arab Federation with Egypt-Syria to counter Britain and Saudi. But this was mainly nominal alliance, with limited practical impact.

events.title: Yemeni Revolution
events.description: Officers inspired by Nasser overthrew Imam Badr (grandson of Yahya), proclaiming the Yemen Arab Republic. But royalists resisted with Saudi support. Egypt sent 70,000 troops supporting republicans, getting stuck in 'Egypt's Vietnam.' Civil war lasted 8 years.

events.title: Aden Emergency
events.description: National Liberation Front (NLF) and Front for Liberation of South Yemen (FLOSY) launched armed struggle against British rule. Guerrilla warfare and terrorist attacks forced British withdrawal. This was part of Arab national liberation movement.

events.title: British Withdrawal from South Yemen
events.description: After years of national liberation struggle, Britain withdrew from Aden. People's Republic of South Yemen established, later renamed People's Democratic Republic of Yemen. This was only Marxist state in Arab world, allied with Soviet Union.

events.title: North Yemen Civil War Ends
events.description: Republicans and royalists reconciled, civil war ended. Saudis recognized Yemen Arab Republic. Tribes and military maintained strong political influence. Ali Abdullah Saleh took power in 1978, ruling North Yemen until unification.

events.title: South Yemen Civil War
events.description: Yemen Socialist Party internal power struggle evolved into brief but bloody civil war, capital Aden saw fierce fighting. About 10,000 died. Conflict weakened South Yemen, paving way for unification.

events.title: Yemeni Unification
events.description: North and South Yemen unified as Republic of Yemen, capital Sana'a. Northern president Saleh became unified Yemen's president, southern leader Beidh vice president. Unification was popular but implementation difficult, two systems and ideologies very different.

events.title: Gulf War Position
events.description: Yemen voted against authorizing use of force against Iraq in UN Security Council, supporting Saddam. This position angered Saudi Arabia and Kuwait, leading to expulsion of about one million Yemeni workers from Gulf countries, severely hitting Yemen's economy.

events.title: Civil War and Southern Secession Attempt
events.description: Unification tensions erupted into civil war. Southern leader Beidh declared secession, but northern forces defeated south in two months. Saleh consolidated power, south was marginalized. This deepened north-south divide, planting seeds for future conflicts.

events.title: Rise of Islamic Extremism
events.description: Saleh used Islamic organizations against socialists, but Islamic radicals gradually lost control. Yemen became jihadist haven. Bin Laden ancestrally Yemeni, al-Qaeda established foothold in Yemen.

events.title: USS Cole Bombing
events.description: Al-Qaeda bombed USS Cole destroyer with explosive boat in Aden port, 17 US sailors died. This attack was major terrorist attack on US before 9/11, exposing Yemen security vulnerabilities and extremist threat.

events.title: Houthi Rebellion Begins
events.description: Zaydi Shia Houthi movement (named after leader Hussein al-Houthi) rebelled in northern Saada province, protesting government discrimination and corruption. Hussein was killed, but his brothers continued rebellion. Yemen government waged six wars trying to suppress Houthis, unsuccessfully.

events.title: Al-Qaeda in Arabian Peninsula
events.description: Yemen and Saudi al-Qaeda branches merged into Al-Qaeda in Arabian Peninsula (AQAP), becoming al-Qaeda's most dangerous branch. AQAP plotted attacks on US, including 2009 Christmas Day bombing attempt. US intensified counterterrorism operations in Yemen, including drone strikes.

events.title: Arab Spring Uprising
events.description: Inspired by Arab Spring, Yemenis massively protested demanding Saleh step down. Protests lasted months, military split, tribes joined opposition. Saleh refused to step down, violent suppression killed hundreds.

events.title: GCC Initiative and Saleh Steps Down
events.description: Under Gulf Cooperation Council mediation, Saleh signed agreement transferring power to Vice President Hadi in exchange for immunity. Saleh stepped down after 33 years rule. But he retained influence, continuing behind-scenes political manipulation.

events.title: Transition Period and National Dialogue
events.description: President Hadi led transition, convening National Dialogue Conference discussing new constitution and federalism. But progress slow, economy deteriorating, security chaotic. Houthis exploited discontent expanding, AQAP active in south, southern separatist movement revived.

events.title: Houthis Capture Sana'a
events.description: Houthi forces advanced south from north, capturing capital Sana'a in September, overthrowing Hadi government. Houthis allied with former President Saleh, using his political network. Hadi fled to southern city Aden.

events.title: Saudi-Led Military Intervention
events.description: Saudi-led Gulf coalition militarily intervened in Yemen, airstrike Houthi targets, supporting Hadi government. Saudis view Houthis as Iranian proxies (Houthis receive Iranian support but relationship is complex). Intervention originally planned to end in weeks, evolved into prolonged war.

events.title: Yemen Civil War and Humanitarian Disaster
events.description: Yemen plunged into devastating civil war, becoming world's worst humanitarian crisis. Saudi coalition airstrikes caused massive civilian casualties, including weddings, funerals and schools. Coalition blockade exacerbated famine and cholera outbreak. Over 370,000 dead (including indirect deaths), millions displaced, 24 million need humanitarian aid. Economy collapsed, currency plummeted, millions face starvation.

events.title: Saleh Killed by Houthis
events.description: Former President Saleh attempted to betray Houthi allies, turning to Saudi camp. Houthi forces attacked Saleh's convoy, killing him. Saleh's death was war turning point, eliminating potential negotiation figure.

events.title: Battle of Hodeidah
events.description: Saudi coalition and Hadi forces attacked Red Sea port Hodeidah, through which 70% of Yemen's imports pass. Fighting threatened food supplies for millions. Under international pressure, sides reached fragile ceasefire, but not fully implemented.

events.title: Southern Transitional Council Conflict
events.description: Southern Transitional Council (STC, seeking South Yemen independence) clashed with Hadi government in Aden, though both allied with Saudi. This highlighted anti-Houthi camp divisions. UAE supported STC, creating rift with Saudi.

events.title: Houthi Attacks on Saudi and Red Sea Shipping
events.description: Houthis used drones and missiles attacking Saudi oil facilities and cities, demonstrating growing military capability (benefiting from Iranian technology). After 2023 Gaza war, Houthis attacked Red Sea shipping in solidarity with Palestine, triggering US-UK military response. Houthis positioned themselves as 'Axis of Resistance' member.

events.title: Brief Ceasefire
events.description: UN brokered two-month ceasefire, longest calm since war began. Fighting significantly reduced, Sana'a airport partially reopened. But ceasefire expired without renewal, though large-scale fighting did not resume, low-intensity conflict continues.

events.title: Ongoing Crisis and Division
events.description: Yemen remains divided: Houthis control north including Sana'a, internationally recognized government controls parts of south (but limited influence), Southern Transitional Council in Aden, AQAP and ISIS in fringe areas. Economy completely collapsed, currency worthless, government employees unpaid for years. 80% population needs humanitarian aid, child malnutrition, lack of healthcare and education. Saudis seek exit but worry about Houthi threat. Yemen called 'forgotten war,' limited international attention. Peace prospects bleak, Yemen faces generational trauma and reconstruction challenges.

events.title: Marib Dam Collapse
events.description: Ancient Marib Dam collapsed (described in Quran), causing large-scale population migration, some tribes migrating north. Dam collapse symbolized end of ancient Yemen prosperity. Dam remained ruins until 20th century reconstruction.

events.title: Qarmatian Movement
events.description: Qarmatian movement (radical Ismaili faction) was active in Yemen, challenging both Abbasid Caliphate and local powers. Movement advocated social equality, attracting many followers.

events.title: Impact of Suez Canal Opening
events.description: Suez Canal opened, Red Sea route became crucial shipping lane, Aden's strategic importance surged. Britain strengthened Aden control, making it key coaling station linking Britain, India and Asia.

events.title: Imam Yahya Assassinated
events.description: Imam Yahya assassinated in coup. His son Ahmad suppressed rebellion, succeeding as new Imam. Ahmad continued authoritarian conservative rule, but faced increasing reform and republican pressure.

events.title: Post-Unification Tensions
events.description: After unification, north-south integration difficult, political and economic conflicts. South felt economically exploited, politically marginalized. Tribal and religious differences deepened divisions.

events.title: Impact of Saudi-Iran Reconciliation
events.description: Saudi Arabia and Iran restored diplomatic relations mediated by China, opening window for Yemen peace talks. Saudis began direct negotiations with Houthis, seeking honorable exit from war. But peace process remains fragile, affected by regional and international factors.

events.title: 沙特-伊朗和解影響
events.description: 在中國斡旋下沙特與伊朗恢復外交關係,為也門和平談判打開窗口。沙特開始與胡塞直接談判,尋求體面退出戰爭。但和平進程仍脆弱,受地區和國際因素影響。...

events.title: 持續危機與分裂
events.description: 也門仍然分裂:胡塞控制北部包括薩那,國際承認的政府控制南部部分地區(但影響力有限),南方過渡委員會在亞丁,AQAP和ISIS在邊緣地區活動。經濟完全崩潰,貨幣無...
